# MultiCore subscription server requirements (llms-full.txt)

> Exactly what a subscription server must do to serve the MultiCore VPN client (1.0.1+), including a server placed in front of a Remnawave panel. Only MultiCore-specific behaviour is covered: generic panel features (users, billing, other clients) are out of scope. Hand this file to a developer or an LLM as the spec.

Human docs (Russian): docs/providers.md, docs/remnawave.md in https://github.com/fatyzzz/multicore-releases.

## 1. Answer three User-Agents on the same URL

MultiCore requests the user's subscription URL and selects the representation by the exact `User-Agent`:

| User-Agent | Must return (2xx) |
|---|---|
| `multicore-json-massive` | JSON array of exactly two elements: `["<Mihomo YAML as a JSON string>", {<Xray JSON object>}]`. Content-Type `application/vnd.multicore.bundle+json; charset=utf-8` |
| `multicore-mihomo` | One complete Mihomo YAML mapping (raw UTF-8 YAML, not JSON, not Base64). Content-Type `application/yaml; charset=utf-8` |
| `multicore-xray` | One complete Xray JSON **object** — never an array, never a JSON string. Content-Type `application/json; charset=utf-8` |

Client behaviour the server must account for:

- `multicore-json-massive` is sent first. A 2xx body whose first non-whitespace byte is `[` is final: the client parses it and makes no further request, even if it is invalid. Serve the bundle correctly or do not serve it (return 404).
- Otherwise the client sends `multicore-mihomo` and `multicore-xray` **in parallel**, so both must come from the same snapshot (see section 5).
- Every other User-Agent belongs to other clients; MultiCore never sends them.

## 2. Pick one of two shapes

**Mihomo-only.** The Mihomo YAML uses only native Mihomo proxies (VLESS/Reality, Trojan, Shadowsocks, Hysteria2, TUIC, ...), and no `socks5` proxy on `127.0.0.1`. Then the Xray half is optional: the client accepts a failed / 404 / non-object `multicore-xray` response and runs an idle Xray. Serving only `multicore-mihomo` is enough.

**Bridged (dual-core).** Some servers need transports Mihomo does not implement, so Xray carries them. For each such server the server must emit a matched triple:

Mihomo proxy:
```yaml
- name: "🇳🇱 Netherlands"      # display name, unique
  type: socks5
  server: 127.0.0.1
  port: 31001                  # unique per subscription
  udp: true
```

Xray inbound + one routing rule into that server's outbound:
```json
{ "tag": "🇳🇱 Netherlands", "listen": "127.0.0.1", "port": 31001, "protocol": "socks",
  "settings": { "auth": "noauth", "udp": true, "ip": "127.0.0.1" } }
{ "type": "field", "inboundTag": ["🇳🇱 Netherlands"], "outboundTag": "mc-nl-1" }
```

Rules for the bridged shape:

- Any Mihomo `socks5` proxy on `127.0.0.1` makes the subscription bridged; the Xray object is then mandatory and must contain an inbound on every such port.
- Inbounds listen on `127.0.0.1` only; ports unique, from a fixed high range (e.g. 31001–31999).
- Exactly one routing rule per bridge, before any catch-all rule.
- The server alone owns the mapping `display name → port → inbound tag → outbound tag`; the client does not build or check it semantically.
- No TUN, DNS policy or process routing in Xray; Mihomo owns those. Keep `direct`/`block` outbounds if needed.
- The client considers Xray ready only when every loopback inbound accepts connections; a bridged Xray object without loopback inbounds never becomes ready.

Native Mihomo proxies and bridges can be mixed in one YAML and in the same groups.

## 3. Mihomo YAML must be the complete client config

- YAML mapping (must not start with `{` or `[`), every proxy and group has a unique `name` and a `type`.
- Contains `tun` (`enable: true`, `auto-route: true`, `auto-detect-interface: true`, `dns-hijack: [any:53]`), `dns` (fake-ip recommended, with `proxy-server-nameserver` so server hostnames resolve outside the tunnel), `proxy-groups`, `rules` ending in `MATCH`.
- `allow-lan: false`; no LAN-reachable ports.
- Do not rely on these keys, the client overrides or removes them: `external-controller*`, `secret`, `external-ui*`, `cors`, `external-doh-server`, `global-client-fingerprint`, `store-selected`, `tun.device`. In its no-TUN mode the client also sets `tun.enable`, `mixed-port`, `bind-address`, `allow-lan`.
- `url-test` groups are shown as "Auto → <current node>"; a top `select` group containing the `url-test` group plus all servers is the recommended layout.
- Optional group icons: `icon: https://…` on a `proxy-groups` entry (PNG/JPEG/WebP/SVG, ≤512 KiB, no redirects); fetched on refresh and shown in the group tabs and tray.
- Reference template: docs/remnawave/multicore-mihomo-template.yaml.

## 4. Headers

Request headers the server receives on every config request (use for device limits):

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `x-hwid` | Stable per-installation id, uppercase UUID (36 chars) |
| `x-device-os` | `windows` / `linux` |
| `x-ver-os` | OS version string |
| `x-device-model` | Device model (`Windows PC` / `Linux PC` fallback) |

Response headers MultiCore reads (send the same set on all three representations):

| Header | Format |
|---|---|
| `subscription-userinfo` | `upload=<bytes>; download=<bytes>; total=<bytes>; expire=<unix s>`; `0` = unlimited |
| `profile-title` | plain or `base64:<b64>`, ≤128 chars |
| `profile-update-interval` | integer hours (default 6, clamped 15 min…30 days) |
| `profile-web-page-url` | http/https |
| `support-url` | http/https/tg |
| `<vendor>-servicelogo` | https image URL; vendor prefix required (e.g. `myvpn-servicelogo`) |
| `announce` | plain or `base64:`, ≤512 chars (`0` hides) |
| `announce-url`, `sub-info-button-text`, `sub-info-color` (`blue`/`green`/`red`) | notice link, label, tone |
| `dumb-mode` (or `<vendor>-dumb-mode`) | `on`/`off` (also `true`/`false`, `1`/`0`), default off; `on` = the app shows only the first `proxy-groups` entry, no group tabs (home and tray); other groups keep working |
| `app-language` (or `<vendor>-app-language`) | `ru`/`en`, any case; regional tags (`en-US`) count as the base language; other values ignored. The active subscription's value sets the UI language; a language the user picked in Settings always wins. Default: the system language |
| `x-hwid-max-devices-reached: true` | device refused; client shows "device limit reached" (send with an empty 200 or with 403) |

Anything else is ignored.

### 4.1 Headers as leading `#` lines of the body (since 1.1.11)

When the server cannot set response headers (static file, gist, object storage, limited panel), write the same headers as comment lines at the very top of the body (Happ/Hiddify/Clash-family convention):

```yaml
#profile-title: base64:8J+agCBGTDg=
#profile-update-interval: 12
#subscription-userinfo: upload=0; download=123; total=1073741824; expire=1798761600
#support-url: https://t.me/support
#profile-web-page-url: https://example.com
#announce: base64:0J/RgNC40LLQtdGC
#dumb-mode: on
#app-language: en
mixed-port: 7890
proxies:
  ...
```

- Keys: every response header above, same names (case-insensitive, `<vendor>-` prefixes included), formats, sanitizers and limits. Not accepted from the body: `content-disposition`, `x-hwid-max-devices-reached`. Unknown keys ignored.
- Line: `#name: value`, spaces allowed after `#` and around `:`; `name` = letters, digits, `-`. Other `#` lines and blank lines are skipped. UTF-8 BOM and CRLF are fine.
- Leading block only: stops at the first line that is neither blank nor `#`, and after 64 lines or 16 KiB. Later `#` lines are plain YAML comments and are not read.
- Bodies: Mihomo YAML (`multicore-mihomo`), Xray JSON (`multicore-xray`), the `multicore-json-massive` bundle (before its `[`), and the Mihomo YAML string inside the bundle. The block is stripped before parsing, so it never reaches the core configs. JSON that does not start with `#` parses exactly as before; a `#` past the leading block is still invalid JSON.
- Priority per key, highest first: (1) real HTTP response headers, (2) leading `#` lines of the `multicore-json-massive` bundle, (3) leading `#` lines of the Mihomo YAML, (4) leading `#` lines of the Xray JSON. A lower source only fills keys no higher source sent (YAML `#app-language: ru` + Xray `#app-language: en` → `ru`; an `app-language` header beats both). A header that was sent owns its key even if its value is invalid.
- Same trust as headers: no extra trust, same sanitizers, never logged.

## 5. Consistency

- All three representations of one refresh must be generated from one immutable snapshot: the bundle halves must equal the standalone answers, and the parallel `multicore-mihomo` / `multicore-xray` answers must match each other (same names, ports, tags).
- If configs are built on demand, build the pair once and serve both halves from a short cache (e.g. 30 s keyed by subscription id + `x-hwid`).
- Recommended: `X-Multicore-Revision: <id shared by all representations>`, `Cache-Control: private, no-cache`.
- Body ≤ 32 MiB per representation. Never log subscription tokens, config bodies or identity headers.

## 6. Checklist

1. `mihomo -t -f mihomo.yaml` passes.
2. Bridged: `xray run -test -config xray.json` passes; every `socks5 127.0.0.1:P` in Mihomo has an Xray inbound on `127.0.0.1:P` with exactly one rule to an existing outbound.
3. Names, tags, ports unique.
4. Bundle is exactly `[string, object]` and equals the standalone answers.
5. Metadata headers present on every representation.

---

## 7. In front of Remnawave

Stock Remnawave (checked against backend v3.4) can serve the **Mihomo-only** shape by itself: a Mihomo template plus a response rule `user-agent EQUALS multicore-mihomo → MIHOMO` (docs/remnawave.md). It cannot serve the **bridged** shape: its `XRAY_JSON` is always an array with one full config per host, and nothing in the panel links Mihomo names to Xray ports. A bridged setup therefore needs a MultiCore subscription server (adapter) in front of Remnawave that does the following.

### 7.1 Panel setup the adapter relies on

- Tag every host that must go through Xray with a host tag, e.g. `MULTICORE_XRAY` (tags match `^[A-Z0-9_:]+$`, ≤36 chars).
- Give hosts unique remarks. Remnawave dedupes duplicates per output with a ` ^~2~^` suffix, and the Mihomo and Xray outputs are filtered differently, so duplicates across the two sets would not line up.
- Response rules (above the default rules), matched on User-Agents only the adapter sends:
  - `user-agent EQUALS multicore-adapter/mihomo` → `MIHOMO`, `subscriptionTemplate: "MultiCore"`, `excludeHostsByTags: ["MULTICORE_XRAY"]`.
  - `user-agent EQUALS multicore-adapter/xray` → `XRAY_JSON`, `subscriptionTemplate: "MultiCore-Xray"` (an Xray JSON template without a `remnawave` injector block, with only `direct`/`block` outbounds).
- Point `SUB_PUBLIC_DOMAIN` (the URL users receive) at the adapter; the adapter talks to the backend at `/api/sub/{shortUuid}`.

### 7.2 Requests to Remnawave

For a MultiCore request on `/…/{shortUuid}` the adapter makes two upstream requests to `GET {backend}/api/sub/{shortUuid}`:

- `User-Agent: multicore-adapter/mihomo` and `User-Agent: multicore-adapter/xray`;
- forward `x-hwid`, `x-device-os`, `x-ver-os`, `x-device-model` unchanged, so Remnawave's HWID limit counts the real device (both requests register the same device);
- set `x-forwarded-for: <client IP>` (Remnawave trusts it unconditionally for the user IP), and strip any client-supplied `x-forwarded-for` / `x-remnawave-real-ip`.

### 7.3 Building the answer

1. **Upstream refusal.** If the Mihomo upstream answer is non-2xx, return that status to every MultiCore UA. If it is `200` with an empty body and `x-hwid-max-devices-reached: true`, return exactly that (empty 200 + its headers) to every MultiCore UA.
2. **Bridged hosts.** Parse the Xray upstream body as a JSON array (Remnawave returns an empty body on a generator error: treat as "no bridges"). Each element is `{...template, outbounds: [<proxy outbound tagged "proxy">, ...template outbounds], remarks: <host remark>}`. A host is bridged when its `remarks` is not a proxy name in the Mihomo answer (the Mihomo answer excluded tagged hosts; hidden hosts are absent from both).
3. **Xray object.** For bridged host *i* in upstream order:
   - port `31001 + i`;
   - outbound = the element's outbound tagged `proxy`, retagged `mc-<i>`; if it references other outbounds of the same element by tag (`proxySettings.tag`, `streamSettings.sockopt.dialerProxy`), copy those too, retagged `mc-<i>-<tag>`, and rewrite the references;
   - inbound `{tag: <remarks>, listen: "127.0.0.1", port, protocol: "socks", settings: {auth: "noauth", udp: true, ip: "127.0.0.1"}}`;
   - rule `{type: "field", inboundTag: [<remarks>], outboundTag: "mc-<i>"}`.
   Result: `{"log":{"loglevel":"warning"},"inbounds":[…],"outbounds":[…bridges, {"tag":"direct","protocol":"freedom"}, {"tag":"block","protocol":"blackhole"}],"routing":{"domainStrategy":"AsIs","rules":[…]}}`. Drop the template's own `inbounds`, `dns` and `routing`.
4. **Mihomo YAML.** Append one `socks5 127.0.0.1:<port>` proxy named `<remarks>` per bridged host. Add these names to every `proxy-groups` entry that already lists at least one Remnawave proxy by name (the groups the template filled), after the existing proxies. Groups using `include-all` pick them up automatically.
5. **No bridged hosts.** Serve the Mihomo answer unchanged and answer `multicore-xray` / `multicore-json-massive` with 404 (Mihomo-only shape).
6. **Serve.**
   - `multicore-json-massive` → `[<Mihomo YAML string>, <Xray object>]`;
   - `multicore-mihomo` → the YAML;
   - `multicore-xray` → the object.
   Cache the built pair ~30 s per `shortUuid + x-hwid` so the parallel requests get the same snapshot. Copy the Mihomo upstream response's metadata headers (`subscription-userinfo`, `profile-title`, `profile-update-interval`, `support-url`, `profile-web-page-url`, `announce*`, `sub-info-*`, `*-servicelogo`, `dumb-mode` / `*-dumb-mode`, `app-language` / `*-app-language`, `content-disposition`, `x-hwid-*`) onto all three answers and add `X-Multicore-Revision`.
7. **Validate before serving.** Run the checks from section 6. On failure, return 502 rather than a half-built pair.

### 7.4 Everything that is not MultiCore

Any request whose `User-Agent` is not one of the three MultiCore values (other apps, browsers, `/info`, the subscription page) is proxied to Remnawave byte-for-byte, headers included. The adapter never changes what other clients receive.

---

## 8. Worked example (bridged, one native + one Xray host)

Mihomo (excerpt):
```yaml
proxies:
  - { name: "🇸🇪 Sweden", type: vless, server: se.example.com, port: 443, uuid: "…", tls: true, network: tcp, flow: xtls-rprx-vision, servername: www.microsoft.com, reality-opts: { public-key: "…", short-id: "…" }, client-fingerprint: chrome }
  - { name: "🇳🇱 Netherlands", type: socks5, server: 127.0.0.1, port: 31001, udp: true }
proxy-groups:
  - { name: "🌍 VPN", type: select, proxies: ["⚡ Автовыбор", "🇸🇪 Sweden", "🇳🇱 Netherlands"] }
  - { name: "⚡ Автовыбор", type: url-test, url: "https://cp.cloudflare.com/generate_204", interval: 300, proxies: ["🇸🇪 Sweden", "🇳🇱 Netherlands"] }
rules:
  - MATCH,🌍 VPN
```

Xray:
```json
{
  "log": { "loglevel": "warning" },
  "inbounds": [
    { "tag": "🇳🇱 Netherlands", "listen": "127.0.0.1", "port": 31001, "protocol": "socks",
      "settings": { "auth": "noauth", "udp": true, "ip": "127.0.0.1" } }
  ],
  "outbounds": [
    { "tag": "mc-0", "protocol": "vless", "settings": { "vnext": [] }, "streamSettings": { "network": "xhttp" } },
    { "tag": "direct", "protocol": "freedom" },
    { "tag": "block", "protocol": "blackhole" }
  ],
  "routing": { "domainStrategy": "AsIs",
    "rules": [ { "type": "field", "inboundTag": ["🇳🇱 Netherlands"], "outboundTag": "mc-0" } ] }
}
```

Bundle for `multicore-json-massive`: `["<the YAML above as one JSON string>", <the object above>]`.
